message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to ask my friend if his dad is going to be there before I agree to hang out with them. Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. I'm 22, still close with my high school friends, and we go out together when I'm home from university. Recently, one of my friends has been bringing his dad along wherever we go. We've been to clubs, and his dad has come along. I've even had him come to my house when my friends were over, which I wasn't expecting. The specific incident that bothered me was when I introduced this group to my current girlfriend. His dad cornered her and forced her into a conversation about cooking and different dishes for half an hour. She was really creeped out by that. Also, this dad isn't bad, but he acts like one of the guys, gets drunk, and engages in locker room talk about women our age. That's really disturbing to me. I've talked to some of the other guys about it, and they think it's cool that his dad hangs out with them and considers him one of the boys. It seems like his dad had his kids really young and missed out on partying with his friends in his early 20s, so now he's doing it with his son and his friends. Now, the next time this group wants to hang out, I really want to ask if the dad is going to be there. I love my friends and still want to hang out with them, but the dad being around all the time is too much. I get it if we're drinking at his house and he wants to hang out, but going out with us or coming to my house without knowing he's coming is an issue. So, is it right or wrong for me to ask my friend if his dad is going to be there before agreeing to hang out? Let me think about the possible perspectives. On one hand, I value my friendships and don't want to cause any conflict. The other guys seem to enjoy having the dad around, and he's making up for lost time. Maybe I'm overreacting, and it's just a phase. But on the other hand, the dad's behavior is making me uncomfortable, especially with my girlfriend. His actions are crossing boundaries, and I don't want to be in situations where that happens again. I also need to consider how to approach this conversation. If I just ask if the dad is coming, it might seem like I'm excluding him, which could hurt my friend's feelings. But I have the right to feel comfortable in my social settings, especially when my girlfriend is involved. It's important to communicate my feelings clearly without making it personal. Another angle is the impact on my girlfriend. Her discomfort is valid, and I should prioritize her feelings as well. If the dad's presence is making her uncomfortable, it's reasonable to want to avoid those situations. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe we can find activities where the dad isn't around, or set boundaries about where we go. But that might be difficult if the dad is insistent on joining. In terms of right or wrong, I think it's more about what's appropriate and respectful. If the dad's presence is making me and my girlfriend uncomfortable, it's reasonable to want to avoid that. It's about setting boundaries to ensure everyone feels safe and respected. So, putting it all together, I think it's okay to ask my friend if his dad is going to be there before agreeing to hang out. It's about protecting my own comfort and that of my girlfriend, and ensuring that our social interactions are enjoyable for everyone involved.
